smoke_notes: User ran flutter run -d macos. Two runtime errors: (1) GET /agent-sessions/agents → 'TypeError: client.agents is not a function' (#703); (2) '[OpencodeClientService] subscribeToEvents error: undefined' + '[OpencodeStreamBridge] No event stream available for directory=/Users/ajhochhalter' (#685) — agent transcript never streamed.
category_name: test asserts shapes production never produces (false-green at the SDK boundary)
root_cause: The hand-written src/@types/opencode-ai-sdk.d.ts declared shapes that do not match the real @opencode-ai/sdk v1.14.49: (a) 'agents' as a top-level client method instead of client.app.agents; (b) event.subscribe as returning the hey-api { data, error } envelope instead of a ServerSentEventsResult = { stream }. Production code followed the d.ts (client.agents(...), raw.data). Tests mocked ABOVE the SDK boundary — the #703 route test stubbed the service method listAgents; the #685 typed-wrapper test's fake client had a shapeless event.subscribe vi.fn() and no app namespace — so neither test ever exercised the real client call. tsc passed because the lie was internally consistent (d.ts ↔ call site).
why_verification_missed_it: verification-gate ran tsc + vitest + flutter, all green, because the d.ts and the tests agreed with each other and with the production call sites. None of them were checked against the real installed SDK surface (node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/gen/sdk.gen.d.ts). This is the exact root-cause #3 the OpenCode parity plan named, recurring because the validation rule 'at least one vitest asserting the SDK spy is invoked with the expected shape' was satisfied with a fake whose shape was also invented.
fix: Corrected the d.ts to the real shapes (app.agents under an app namespace; event.subscribe → Promise<{ stream }> with no envelope); fixed both call sites (client.app.agents, return raw consuming raw.stream). Added opc_sdk_boundary_regression.test.ts: 4 tests mocking the REAL SDK shapes that fail on the pre-fix code. Cross-checked ALL other M3/M4 wrappers (session.*, mcp.*) against the real Session/Mcp classes — all method paths correct.
prevention: When hand-authoring an SDK .d.ts, every declared method/return shape MUST be diffed against the real installed SDK's generated types (node_modules/.../sdk.gen.d.ts), not assumed. Boundary tests must build fakes from the REAL shape (e.g. ServerSentEventsResult = { stream }, not an envelope) — a fake invented to match the d.ts re-encodes the same lie. event.subscribe is the one endpoint that does NOT use the { data, error } envelope.

workflow_adherence.gate_outcome: PASS (false-green — green tsc/vitest/flutter against self-consistent but wrong types)
workflow_adherence.note: All checks were green; the gap was that no check compared the hand-written d.ts to the real SDK. Resolved by adding real-shape boundary tests.
